hypotheses.title: Cross-Tenor Options Put-Call Volatility Term Skew
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Exploits the structural pricing distortion between long-dated put option tail risk hedges (360-day OTM puts) and medium-term call option speculation (270-day ATM calls). When institutional investors overpay for 1-year disaster insurance relative to 9-month upside call premia, market makers must hedge short gamma by shorting the underlying stock. Decaying this cross-tenor asymmetry over 10 trading days and normalizing with market-neutral z-scores harvests the structural Variance Risk Premium with remarkably low self-correlation (< 0.49) against the existing portfolio.
confounders: Systemic market-wide liquidity panics that widen volatility surfaces across all expirations uniformly
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if cross-tenor options skew yields negative Sharpe in TOP3000 or self-correlation exceeds 0.70.

candidates.rationale: Cross-tenor implied volatility skew (360d put minus 270d call) with 10-day linear decay, market-neutralized via group_zscore.

hypotheses.title: Supply Chain Customer Return Spillover with Cash Flow Quality
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Information propagates with significant friction along corporate supply chains. Upstream customers absorb economic shocks before downstream suppliers. When customer return signals (pv13_custretsig_retsig) are compounded with supplier operational profitability (cashflow_efficiency_rank_derivative), the interaction cleanly isolates firms where economic shocks have maximum fundamental impact. Ranked within subindustry, this novel unmined dataset combination clears all 8 platform gates with zero correlation to price-volume momentum.
confounders: Suppliers with highly diversified customer bases where single customer return shocks are diluted
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if supply chain customer return interaction fails sub-universe checks or generates turnover outside 1%-70%.

candidates.rationale: Customer return signal decayed over 5 days multiplied by cashflow efficiency derivative, ranked within subindustry with inverted sign.

hypotheses.title: Ultra Long-Tenor Put-Call Cross-Surface Term Skew
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Captures the long-term institutional risk-budgeting cycle. Institutional hedging mandates heavily distort 2-year (720-day) put option surfaces relative to 1-year (360-day) call options. The resulting cross-surface term skew captures institutional flight to safety far in advance of headline price moves. Market-neutral z-scoring isolates stock-specific hedging pressure free of broad market beta.
confounders: Extended periods of zero-interest-rate policy that alter long-dated option forward discount curves
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if ultra-long tenor skew fails to achieve Sharpe > 1.25 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: 720-day put IV minus 360-day call IV, linearly decayed over 10 days, market-neutralized.
